name: Lana Del Rey
label: Interscope / Polydor
lede: Elizabeth Grant made one album as Lizzy Grant and watched her label pull it, then put a self-edited webcam video online and came back as Lana Del Rey. Her ninth album, Ocean Blvd, ranked No. 11 on Pitchfork's 2023 list.

eras.title: Lizzy Grant, before the name
eras.text: A Manhattan-born Fordham philosophy student records as May Jailer and Lizzy Grant, signs with 5 Points, and sees her album pulled within months. Almost nobody hears any of it.

years.h: As May Jailer, Elizabeth Grant records an acoustic album, Sirens
years.p: It never came out, and it is the earliest recording in her catalog.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, she was born in Manhattan on June 21, 1985, and earned a philosophy degree at Fordham University in 2008. Sirens stayed off the market.

years.h: The Kill Kill EP carries the name Lizzy Grant
years.p: Two years before the self-titled album, the name on the cover was still Lizzy Grant.
years.xp: The self-titled 2010 album's cover would later carry the line "Lana Del Ray A.K.A. Lizzy Grant", which nods to the name she used on the 2008 EP, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lana Del Ray (album) · Wikipedia: Lana Del Rey
years.h: Lana Del Ray lands on iTunes, then vanishes within months
years.p: Producer David Kahne recorded the 13 tracks with her over three months in 2008. The spelling nodded to actress Lana Turner and the Ford Del Rey sedan.
years.xp:
5 Points Records released it through iTunes and Amazon MP3, then pulled it within three months of an April 1, 2010 separation agreement. Del Rey has said the label "was unable to fund it", per Wikipedia.

After Born to Die, she said in January 2012 she would re-release it once she owned the rights. That never happened. Only "Yayo" was officially reworked, on the 2012 Paradise EP, and the album exists now as bootlegs and digital archives.

years.cap: Del Rey at Bowery Ballroom, New York
years.h: Ben Mawson and Ed Millett become her managers, and she moves to London
years.p: They took her on after the 5 Points deal fell apart.

eras.title: A webcam, an SNL spot, and a lot of noise
eras.text: One self-made video sets the machine going. An SNL performance turns the backlash into a national argument, and Born to Die sells anyway.

years.cap: Del Rey at Paradiso, Amsterdam, November 2011
years.src: Wikipedia: Video Games (Lana Del Rey song) · Wikipedia: Born to Die (album)
years.h: She edits her own webcam video for Video Games, and it spreads
years.p: The video stitches webcam footage of her to archive clips and paparazzi footage. Justin Parker co-wrote the song; Robopop produced it at BMG Studios in New York.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, she put the song out with no plan to promote it as a single. It went viral on YouTube, was picked up for The CW's Ringer in September 2011, and came out through Stranger Records that June.

Interscope and Polydor signed her that November, and the song was re-released on October 7, 2011 as the lead single from Born to Die. Pitchfork named it Best New Music. It won the 2012 Ivor Novello for Best Contemporary Song.

years.h: Q names her "Next Big Thing" weeks before Interscope signs her
years.p: The trophy arrived in October 2011; the joint Interscope and Polydor signing followed in November.

q: never had a persona. Never needed one. Never will.
years.src: Wikipedia: Born to Die (album) · Wikipedia: Lana Del Rey · Consequence: Lana Del Rey Headlines Coachella
years.h: Her SNL debut turns into a national argument
years.p: NBC anchor Brian Williams used those words about her performance of "Video Games" and "Blue Jeans". Cast member Andy Samberg and host Daniel Radcliffe defended her.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Samberg and Radcliffe put the negativity down to her past and her family, not the performance itself. In 2024 she brought the moment back on purpose: her Coachella set included a hologram performance she framed as a callback to SNL.

years.cap: Del Rey at Irving Plaza, New York, June 2012
years.h: Born to Die reaches No. 2 and sells 3.4 million in 2012
years.p: Emile Haynie, Rick Nowels and Robopop produced most of it, across studios from London to Electric Lady.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists it as the world's fifth best-selling album of 2012. Pitchfork's first score was 5.5; the site rescored it more warmly in 2021, calling it "thrillingly rich", per Wikipedia. Metacritic has it at 62 from 37 reviews.

By December 2025 it had spent 618 weeks on the Billboard 200, the longest run by a female artist, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lana Del Rey · Wikipedia: Lana Del Ray (album)
years.h: A new EP, Paradise, opens at No. 10 on the Billboard 200
years.p: It carried "Yayo", reworked from the shelved 2010 album, alongside the Born to Die tracks.

eras.title: A remix, a short film, and a trip to Nashville
eras.text: A remix her label didn't want makes her a radio star, a short film she wrote and starred in introduces the next album, and Dan Auerbach moves the sound to guitars. Honeymoon goes back to strings.

years.h: Her label doesn't want Cedric Gervais's remix, and it becomes her biggest US hit
years.p: The "Summertime Sadness" remix went to No. 1 on Beatport, then on to BBC Radio 1 and the Billboard Hot 100 at No. 6.
years.xp: The original came out June 22, 2012, produced by Emile Haynie and Rick Nowels. Gervais's version became her highest-charting US single at No. 6 and won the 2014 Grammy for Best Remixed Recording, Non-Classical, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lana Del Rey · Wikipedia: Ultraviolence (album) · Wikipedia: Lana Del Rey videography
years.h: At the Cinerama Dome she premieres Tropico and names her next album
years.p: Anthony Mandler directed the short film she wrote and starred in. The title she announced that night was Ultraviolence.
years.xp: The title comes from Anthony Burgess's novella A Clockwork Orange, per Wikipedia. Earlier in 2013 she had also released "Young and Beautiful" for The Great Gatsby soundtrack.

years.h: Dan Auerbach books three days; Ultraviolence takes six weeks
years.p: Auerbach of the Black Keys recorded her live at his Easy Eye Sound studio in Nashville.
years.xp: It opened at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 and topped charts in 12 countries. Auerbach said every criticism he had heard about her was proven wrong in the studio, per Wikipedia. Pitchfork scored it 7.1; Metacritic 74.

years.h: Her sister photographs the Honeymoon cover from a tour bus
years.p: Chuck Grant shot it on a Los Angeles Starline bus after a session with Neil Krug felt off. The album entered at No. 2.
years.xp: Rick Nowels and Kieron Menzies produced it in Santa Monica and New York. It sold 116,000 units in its first US week, per Wikipedia. Pitchfork gave it 7.5 and Metacritic 78.

eras.title: Guests, a dispute, and the peak
eras.text: Lust for Life fills the record with guests and daylight. Norman Fucking Rockwell!, made with Jack Antonoff, earns an Album of the Year nomination and lands on more critics' 2019 lists than any other album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lust for Life (Lana Del Rey album)
years.h: Lust for Life opens at No. 1 in the US and UK, with The Weeknd and Stevie Nicks
years.p: A$AP Rocky, Playboi Carti and Sean Ono Lennon also appear.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 7.7 and said it presented the "sad girl" as, could it be, happy. It earned a Best Pop Vocal Album nomination at the 2018 Grammys, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Radiohead and Del Rey dispute whether "Get Free" echoes "Creep"
years.p: According to Wikipedia, the dispute ended in summer 2017.

years.cap: Del Rey at the Grammy Museum, Los Angeles, October 2019
q: This is the American dream, right now.
years.src: Wikipedia: Norman Fucking Rockwell! · Wikipedia: Lana Del Rey videography
years.h: Jack Antonoff co-writes Norman Fucking Rockwell!, and Pitchfork gives it a 9.4
years.p: Pitchfork's Jenn Pelly called her one of America's greatest living songwriters. It debuted at No. 3 in the US and No. 1 in the UK.
years.xp:
Jack Antonoff produced it with Zach Dawes, Andrew Watt and Rick Nowels contributing. Metacritic scored it 87 and counted it the most-named album on 2019 year-end critic lists.

The Album of the Year nomination at the 62nd Grammys followed. Rolling Stone later placed it at No. 321 on its 500 Greatest Albums list. The title track's video was directed by her sister Chuck Grant.

eras.title: Two albums in 2021, and a car break-in
eras.text: She moves into books and a spoken-word release, then puts out two albums seven months apart. A break-in in 2022 takes hard drives and a manuscript.

years.h: Violet Bent Backwards over the Grass arrives as an audiobook first
years.p: Jack Antonoff produced the spoken-word recording. The physical poetry book followed on September 29.

years.src: Wikipedia: Chemtrails over the Country Club
years.h: Chemtrails over the Country Club closes on a Joni Mitchell cover
years.p: Weyes Blood and Zella Day sing on "For Free". The album reached No. 1 in the UK, her fifth chart-topper there.
years.xp: Nikki Lane appears on "Breaking Up Slowly". Pitchfork scored it 7.5 and Metacritic 81, per Wikipedia. It was the UK's fastest-selling vinyl of the century for a female act.

years.h: Blue Banisters arrives seven months after Chemtrails
years.p: It reached No. 8 in the US and No. 2 in the UK, with Zach Dawes, Drew Erickson and Rick Nowels among the producers.
years.xp: Pitchfork scored it 7.7. In a March 2023 Rolling Stone UK interview she said she made it as a response to accusations about cultural appropriation and glamorizing domestic abuse, per Wikipedia, and kept its promotion minimal.

years.h: Thieves take her laptop and a 200-page manuscript from a car
years.p: Per Wikipedia, the theft also included hard drives, camcorders and unfinished songs. The manuscript was titled Behind the Iron Gates - Insights from an Institution.

years.h: Taylor Swift's Midnights gets a Del Rey duet, "Snow on the Beach"
years.p: The track debuted at No. 4 on the Hot 100. A remix with an expanded Del Rey verse followed on May 26, 2023.

eras.title: Ocean Blvd
eras.text: Her ninth album is built from voice memos, arrives two weeks late, and ends up on critics' year-end lists and the Grammy ballot for Album of the Year.

years.h: "A&W" changes genre halfway through
years.p: Pitchfork's Shaad D'Souza named it Best New Track. Recorded in two days, it moves from an acoustic first half to a trap-flavored second half fans call "Jimmy".
years.xp: Antonoff has said the second part began as an outtake from the 2018 Norman Fucking Rockwell! sessions. The song was nominated for Song of the Year at the 66th Grammys.

years.cap: Did You Know That There's a Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd
years.src: Wikipedia: Did You Know That There's a Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd · Album of the Year: Lana Del Rey - Did you know
years.h: Ocean Blvd is Best New Music, then No. 11 on Pitchfork's 2023 list
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.3. Its Olivia Horn called it a "sweeping, sterling, often confounding work".
years.xp:
She recorded raw vocal takes into her phone and sent them to Drew Erickson for orchestral arrangements. Mike Hermosa added piano, and Jack Antonoff arrived late. Guests include Jon Batiste, Father John Misty, SYML, Tommy Genesis and Bleachers, plus a sermon by Judah Smith. The title refers to the Jergins Tunnel in Long Beach, California, built in 1927 and closed in 1967.

The album was delayed from March 10 to March 24. It went to No. 1 in the UK and No. 3 in the US, with 41,000 and 115,000 units, per Wikipedia. Metacritic scores it 80. The Daily Telegraph's Neil McCormick called it boring, citing dull production and shapeless songs.

Photographer Neil Krug shot 65 candidate cover images. A nude photo she rejected for the standard cover was later used on limited vinyl editions.

years.h: A Waffle House shift in Florence, Alabama
years.p: Employee uniform and all, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Did You Know That There's a Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd · Wikipedia: Lana Del Rey
years.h: Five Grammy nominations, led by Album of the Year for Ocean Blvd
years.p: The album was also up for Best Alternative Music Album at the 66th Grammys.

eras.title: Stadiums and a country record
eras.text: She headlines Coachella and Fenway, records with Quavo and The Weeknd, tours UK stadiums, and works on a country album whose title keeps changing.

years.cap: Lana Del Rey - Primavera Sound, Barcelona - Friday 31st May 2024 · Wikimedia
years.src: Consequence: Lana Del Rey Headlines Coachella · Wikipedia: Lana Del Rey
yt: Lana Del Rey and Billie Eilish, Video Games, Coachella 2024
years.h: Billie Eilish joins her on a gilded balcony at her first Coachella headline set
years.p: They sang "Ocean Eyes" and "Video Games" while Jon Batiste played keys and Del Rey pole-danced.
years.xp: She had first played Coachella in 2014. Antonoff played piano during the hologram number, per Consequence. Eilish said Del Rey "is the reason for half you bitches' existence, including mine"; the set ran 20 songs and revived rarities including a Sublime cover.

years.h: Fenway Park sells out for her first solo stadium show
years.p: She announced the date in April, the same month as Coachella.

years.h: Quavo joins her on "Tough", a first taste of the country album
years.p: She had announced the tenth album on January 31, 2024. Its title has changed from Lasso to The Right Person Will Stay to Stove.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the title as Stove, confirmed in January 2026, with "Henry, Come On" and "Bluebird" released in spring 2025.

years.cap: Del Rey at Wembley Stadium, London, July 3, 2025
years.h: Six stadium dates across the UK and Ireland, with Addison Rae opening
years.p: Wembley, Cardiff, Glasgow, Liverpool and Dublin were among them. London Grammar and Banks also opened.

years.h: She writes "First Light" for the 007: First Light video game
years.p: She worked with composer David Arnold on the James Bond tie-in.
